llm.summary: The skill's behavior (making calls via Pine Voice) is plausible, but the SKILL.md requests credentials and uses a staging API host while the registry metadata claims no required environment variables and provides no authoritative source — these mismatches and the need to transmit sensitive info make the package inconsistent and worth extra caution.

dimensions.detail: The skill's stated purpose (make real phone calls via Pine Voice) matches the runtime instructions (curl requests to Pine's voice API). However, registry metadata claims no required env vars or credentials while SKILL.md clearly requires PINE_ACCESS_TOKEN and PINE_USER_ID — this inconsistency is unexpected and reduces trust. The skill also points to a staging API host (agent3-api-gateway-staging.19pine.ai) instead of an obvious production endpoint.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: Instructions explicitly tell the agent to run curl via exec, include Authorization headers using env vars, gather potentially sensitive personal/payment/account data from the user, and spawn background polling sessions (sessions_spawn). While these actions align with making phone calls and returning transcripts, the SKILL.md also instructs the agent to access env vars that the registry did not declare — an instruction-scope mismatch. The use of a staging gateway URL is also unexpected in a published skill.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: This is an instruction-only skill with no install spec and no code files, so nothing is written to disk or fetched during install. That lowers installation risk. The runtime relies on curl via exec, which is normal for instruction-only integrations.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill requires two credentials (PINE_ACCESS_TOKEN and PINE_USER_ID) according to SKILL.md — that is reasonable for a third-party voice API. But the registry metadata lists no required env vars, creating a discrepancy. Additionally, the skill encourages collecting sensitive information (account numbers, payment info) that will be transmitted to Pine; users must understand and approve sending such data to the third party. The staging API hostname increases suspicion about whether this is a production, supported integration.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill does not request always:true and does not claim to modify agent/system configs. It asks the agent to use sessions_spawn to run background polling for potentially long durations — this is functionally necessary for long calls but does increase the window during which an autonomous sub-agent is active. Autonomous invocation is platform default; on its own this is not a high privilege, but combine it with credential use and sensitive data transmission and it merits caution.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: Do not install blindly. Before using: (1) verify the vendor (19pine.ai) and confirm that the production API endpoint is legitimate — the SKILL.md points at a 'staging' gateway which is unusual; (2) insist the registry metadata be updated to declare required env vars (PINE_ACCESS_TOKEN, PINE_USER_ID) so you know what secrets you'll provide; (3) avoid sending highly sensitive data (full payment card numbers, passwords) unless you have read and accepted Pine's privacy/security policy and you trust the endpoint; (4) use a scoped, revocable token for PINE_ACCESS_TOKEN and rotate it after testing; (5) prefer a skill that documents an official homepage, support contact, and production API endpoints — if those are not provided, treat the integration as higher risk. If you want higher assurance, ask the skill publisher to (a) correct registry metadata to list required env vars, (b) confirm the API base URL is production (not staging), and (c) provide an authoritative homepage or vendor contact.
